_readme: The places a mission can go. Each destination has an id (for example mars_orbit) and a list of facts. Every fact is written as { "value": ..., "source": ... } so you can see where it came from. A source is a link to NASA, a written game-design choice, or the word PLACEHOLDER (made up for now; a student replaces it before the final submission). arrival_type = how the spacecraft ends its trip: "orbit" (circle the planet), "surface" (land) or "flyby" (fly past). crew = true if people travel on a ship that carries the spacecraft you build. The words on the screen (names, descriptions) are in data/story.json. MORE FACTS (batch 7): distance_from_sun_au and distance_from_sun_million_km = how far from the Sun. sunlight_vs_earth = how strong the sunlight is compared with Earth (1.0 = Earth, 0.43 = less than half as strong). signal_delay_minutes = how long a radio message takes one way: min = planets closest, max = planets farthest. what_makes_it_different = one line (the words on the screen are in story.json). materials = what a surface site has (ids; their names are in story.json). landing_window_tightness = how tight the landing presses are at that site (1.0 = normal, bigger = tighter). pickable_arrival_types in game_data.json says which arrival types can be chosen yet.

arrival_type.source: Game-design choice: this mission is a Mars orbiter, like NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO), which circled Mars to map it.

crew.source: Written game-design choice by Kaleb (AGENT_SOURCE.md section 2, 2026-11-10): Mars missions have a crew on a ship that carries the spacecraft the player built.

trip_days.source: PLACEHOLDER. NASA's MRO launched in Aug 2005 and reached Mars in March 2006 (about 7 months; the MRO launch press kit is already cited in game_data.json), but the exact quote and day count are not written down in this project yet. A student checks the press kit and replaces 210 with a quoted number: https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/press_kits/mro-launch-Aug05.pdf

what_makes_it_different.value: Low ground: more air to slow the landing
what_makes_it_different.source: PLACEHOLDER idea (GAME_PLAN.md section 4: low ground, more air to slow the landing). It is NOT verified: no NASA page we read says Gale's low height gives thicker air, so the game text does not claim it. A student finds a NASA source or removes the idea. What NASA does say: Gale is 96 miles (154 km) wide and holds a layered mountain about 3 miles (5 km) tall, https://science.nasa.gov/resource/gale-crater-future-home-of-mars-rover-curiosity/

distance_from_sun_au.source: Worked out from NASA Jupiter Fact Sheet: semimajor axis 778.479 million km divided by Earth's 149.598 million km (Mars Fact Sheet) = 5.20 AU. Europa circles Jupiter, so it is the same distance from the Sun. https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/jupiterfact.html

signal_delay_minutes.source: Worked out from NASA Jupiter Fact Sheet Earth-Jupiter distances (min 588.5, max 968.5 million km) divided by the speed of light 299,792 km/s: about 32.7 and 53.8 minutes one way. https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/jupiterfact.html

trip_days.source: ESTIMATE worked out from NASA's Europa Clipper page: launched Oct. 14, 2024, reaches Jupiter in "April 2030" (NASA gives no day, so the 15th of April 2030 is ASSUMED; the answer is about 2,009 days). https://science.nasa.gov/mission/europa-clipper/
